Anthropic.title: Tools and environments - Claude.ai Documentation
Anthropic.content:
Claude writes and runs Python, R, and shell commands.

Claude writes and runs Python, R, and shell commands (PowerShell on Windows). Python and R run in a persistent kernel that keeps variables in memory across steps in a session. The kernel ends after about 30 minutes idle, when a package install restarts its environment, or when the session ends.

Starter environments

First launch creates two read-only conda environments in ~/.claude-science:

When work needs packages the starters don’t have, Claude reuses an existing named environment or proposes creating a new one (for example, single-cell or structural-biology). A permission card shows the environment name and initial packages. Environments are shared across all projects on the machine. To list or delete environments, ask Claude; there’s no settings page for them.

Installing packages

Claude installs from these sources by default:

Conda: micromamba from the conda-forge, bioconda, defaults, and pytorch channels

Python: pip from PyPI

R: CRAN and Bioconductor

To have conda and pip download packages from an internal mirror instead, see Point package installs at an internal mirror.A package installed into an environment is permanent and available in every session and project using that environment. A package installed inline in a code cell (pip install or install.packages()) lasts only until the kernel restarts. To keep a package, ask Claude to install it into the environment. For a Python package Claude can’t install there with pip, see Python package sources for starter and task environments.For tools without a package, Claude downloads source, builds it in the sandbox with compilers from conda-forge, and saves the build as an artifact for reuse.The sandbox has no root access or system package manager. apt and sudo aren’t available; Claude uses conda-forge or builds from source instead.

Python package sources for starter and task environments

When Claude uses pip to install a Python package into a starter or task environment, it installs only prebuilt packages (wheels) from PyPI or, if one is set up, your internal mirror. It doesn’t install a package from a git repository, a web address, a local folder, or a local file. If the package, or a package it depends on, has no wheel for your computer and Python version, the install fails. That includes a package published only as source code. In a Windows starter environment, if only a dependency has no wheel, the package installs without any of its dependencies. Ask Claude to install the others by name.When the newest version of a package has no wheel for your computer and Python version but an older version does, pip installs the older version. To find out which version you have, ask Claude. If you need the newest version, use one of the ways below.To use a package Claude can’t install this way, ask Claude to install it into the environment with conda if conda-forge has it. On macOS and Linux, starter environments refuse some conda packages, such as sphinx and some tensorflow builds, so have Claude install those into a task environment. If conda-forge doesn’t have the package, ask Claude to install it with pip in a code cell, where it lasts only until the kernel restarts.

Environments in granted folders

Code Claude runs can read granted folders but can’t change anything in them, including Python and conda environments from any tool (see Sandbox).Claude can run code from an environment there unless its Python is somewhere the sandbox can’t read, such as ~/.local/share/uv. Claude can’t create environments there or change their packages.On Linux, pip, uv, and pixi fail with Read-only file system, and conda with EnvironmentNotWritableError. In a uv project, uv run and uv sync fail the same way whenever they have to update the environment, for example after pyproject.toml changes. To skip that update, ask Claude to use uv run --no-sync.To add packages, choose one of these:

Ask Claude to use a task environment instead. Packages installed there stay available in every session and project that uses it.

In a uv project, ask Claude to use a separate environment. Have Claude set UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT to the full path of a folder in the session’s workspace folder and install packages there with uv pip install --python. The variable must stay set for later uv commands, including uv run. uv add and uv remove still fail because they change project files, and uv run can fail in projects that build with setuptools. The separate environment belongs to that session, so another session starts without it. It’s cleared with the workspace folder (see A file that Claude made is gone). For a change every session keeps, change the environment yourself in a terminal outside Claude Science.

Change the environment yourself. In a terminal outside Claude Science, use the tool’s own commands to add, update, or remove packages.

GPUs

If your Linux machine has NVIDIA GPUs, the sandbox makes them available to code Claude runs, including on multi-GPU machines. To use them, turn on the Host GPU switch in Settings > Compute. Sessions you start after that can use the GPU. A session started while the switch was off keeps running without it, and so does a session continued from it with Continue as a new session.

Turning on the Host GPU switch reduces the default sandboxing configuration applied by Claude Science. Code in GPU sessions uses your graphics driver directly.

If Claude Science finds no GPU, Claude notes this when a task needs one and can run the work on the remote compute you’ve connected. See Remote compute clusters and Compute providers. If your machine has an NVIDIA GPU but the Host GPU switch isn’t in Settings > Compute, or Claude says there’s no GPU in a session started with the switch on, see How Claude Science detects a GPU.

How Claude Science detects a GPU

On Linux, Claude Science detects an NVIDIA GPU by running nvidia-smi. When it finds no GPU this way, Claude treats the machine as having no GPU, and the Host GPU switch doesn’t appear in Settings > Compute unless it’s already on.Claude Science runs the first nvidia-smi it finds in these folders, in this order:

/usr/local/nvidia/bin

/usr/bin

/bin

/usr/lib/wsl/lib

/opt/bin

To see which folder yours is in, run command -v nvidia-smi in a terminal outside Claude Science. Claude Science doesn’t look for nvidia-smi in any other folder, such as /usr/local/bin. If the nvidia-smi in a listed folder is a link, the file it finally leads to, after any other links, must also be named nvidia-smi and be under /usr, /lib, /lib64, /bin, /sbin, or /opt. To see the file a link finally leads to, run readlink -f with its path, for example readlink -f /usr/bin/nvidia-smi.nvidia-smi also has to work without the LD_LIBRARY_PATH environment variable, because Claude Science doesn’t pass that variable on to it, even when your terminal has it set. To check, run it in a terminal outside Claude Science by its full path with the variable removed, for example env -u LD_LIBRARY_PATH /usr/bin/nvidia-smi. If that fails where plain nvidia-smi works, the variable is the reason. Make nvidia-smi work without the variable, or ask your system administrator to.If nvidia-smi is in another folder, link it into /usr/bin, which takes administrator (sudo) access. If you don’t have that access, ask your system administrator to make the link. For example, when nvidia-smi is in /usr/local/bin, run this in a terminal outside Claude Science:

After either fix is in place, run claude-science stop in a terminal outside Claude Science and start Claude Science again. If Claude Science then finds the GPU, the Host GPU switch is in Settings > Compute and its label shows the GPU’s name. Turn it on if it’s off, then start a new session, not one made with Continue as a new session.

# The Claude Ecosystem: One AI, Many Ways to Work

Most people know Claude the same way: a chat box, a question typed in, an answer typed back. That picture used to be accurate. Today it is incomplete.

Over the last two years, Anthropic has built a full platform around its models. Claude can now write and edit code across entire repositories, control web browsers, operate desktop applications, connect directly to tools like Jira, Slack, and GitHub, and run scheduled jobs in the cloud with no human present.

This growth has created a real problem for newcomers: too many names and too little guidance. Connectors, MCP, skills, plugins, routines, computer use, sub-agents, dynamic workflows: it is hard to know how any of it relates.

This blog explains the whole ecosystem in plain language. It assumes no prior knowledge, defines every term the first time it appears, and is honest about what does not work well yet. Product details are accurate as of November 13, 2026.

## What is the Claude Ecosystem

The Claude ecosystem is a family of AI models, plus the products, integrations, and automation tools built on top of them. The idea behind it is simple: the same AI capability should be reachable from wherever your work happens.

In simple terms, everything in the ecosystem answers one of three questions:

- Where do I meet Claude?

Where Do I Meet Claude? Different people work in different places, so Claude appears as a chat and work app, a command-line tool, a browser extension, and an agent inside tools like Slack and Microsoft 365.

- What can Claude touch?

An AI that cannot reach your ticket queue, your browser, or your files can only give advice. Extensions give Claude the ability to act.

- Do I have to be there?

The autonomy features gradually remove the need for you to supervise every step, until work happens while you sleep.

One clarification saves a lot of confusion later: the ecosystem is not one product. There is no single application that contains all of this. It is a set of products that share the same underlying models and the same open standards.

## How the Claude Ecosystem Differs from a Simple Chatbot

A simple chatbot answers what you paste in; the ecosystem reaches your tools and can keep working without you.

## How the Claude Ecosystem Works

Nearly every interaction, from a casual chat to an autonomous overnight run, follows the same five-step pattern.

### Step 1: Intent

You state a goal in plain language, such as: “A new refund screen has been built. Test it.”

### Step 2: Context

Claude gathers what it needs to understand the task: your files, the relevant tickets, your project conventions, and any connected tools.

### Step 3: Reasoning

The model plans the work and decides what to do first, which tools to use, and how to handle problems.

### Step 4: Action

Claude acts on the plan through its extensions: it edits files, clicks through screens, calls APIs, and runs commands.

### Step 5: Verification

The result is checked. Sometimes by you, sometimes by a test, and sometimes by another AI agent.

What changes between a simple chat and a fully autonomous run is not this shape. It is who performs Step 5, and how many times the loop repeats. In chat, you verify the answer yourself. The four common modes compare like this:

A /goal condition works only when it can be checked. “All tests in the refund suite pass” works; “the feature is production-ready” does not, because no command can prove it.

## Architecture of the Claude Ecosystem

The Claude ecosystem can be understood through five key layers.

Models sit at the base, each layer above builds on the one below, and governance applies to all of them. Below are the five layers:

1.The Models (Foundation): Everything is powered by the models. The main Claude models are:

a. Haiku: Fast and low-cost for simple tasks.

b. Sonnet: Balanced for everyday coding, analysis, and writing.

c. Opus: More powerful for complex tasks requiring higher accuracy.

d. Fable: A Mythos-tier model, a step above Opus, for complex reasoning, coding, research, and agentic work.

Fable shares its underlying model with Claude Mythos and adds safety measures for biology and cybersecurity. Mythos itself is not publicly available; a small group of organizations use it through Project Glasswing.

2.Surfaces (Where You Work): As of November 13, 2026, These are different ways to interact with Claude.

a. Claude App: Chat, upload files, work in projects, and hand off longer tasks that produce finished documents, slides, and designs, without a terminal.

b. Claude Code: Helps developers understand, edit, test, and manage code, from the terminal, web, desktop, and mobile.

c. Claude Science: • A research workbench for scientists, run on the lab’s own machines.

d. Claude Design: Creates prototypes, wireframes, and designs from descriptions.

e. Claude API and Console: For developers building Claude into their own products.

3.Extensions (How Claude Reaches Your Tools): These allow Claude to interact with external tools and applications.

a. Connectors and MCP: Also known as Model Context Protocol, connects Claude with systems such as Jira, GitHub, and Slack, etc.

b. Skills: Tell Claude how to perform specific tasks according to team guidelines.

c. Plugins: Bundle skills, commands, and connectors into one installable package, such as a browser-testing kit.

d. Claude for Chrome: Allows Claude to interact with websites.

e. Computer Use: Allows Claude to control desktop applications using the mouse and keyboard.

4. Autonomy (Running Without You): This layer reduces the need for continuous human supervision. All four features below are part of Claude Code.

a. Goals: The /goal command repeats work until a stated condition is met, with an evaluator model checking after each turn.

b. Sub-agents: Multiple helper agents work on different tasks in parallel.

## Get Vijay Singh’s stories in your inbox

Join Medium for free to get updates from this writer.

c. Dynamic Workflows: • Claude writes its own orchestration script and coordinates tens to hundreds of parallel sub-agents for large tasks such as codebase-wide migrations.

d. Routines: Run tasks automatically on cloud, triggered by a schedule an API call, or a GitHub event, even when your laptop is closed.

5. Governance (Security and Trust): This layer helps organizations use Claude safely.

a. Sandboxing: Runs agent tasks in controlled environments.

b. Permission Gates: Requests permission before accessing files or services in interactive sessions.

c. Enterprise Controls: SSO and role-based access control. Admins can also switch off routines and dynamic workflows for the whole organization.

d. Data Protection: Controls for protecting company data, with no training on business data under commercial terms.

## Use Case: Testing a New Feature from a Jira Ticket

### Overview

A QA team receives a new screen to test: a premium-refund feature. Normally this means reading the ticket, writing test cases, automating them, running them, and updating three different systems by hand. Here is the same job inside the Claude ecosystem. Each step names its stage in the five-step loop and the parts of the ecosystem it uses.

### Step-by-Step Process

### Step 1: The Request(Intent)

The tester asks Claude Code to test a new feature in a Jira ticket.

### Step 2: Gathering Context(Context)

Claude reads the Jira ticket, acceptance criteria through a Jira connector, and team testing guidelines through a skill.

### Step 3: Planning(Reasoning)

Claude prepares a test plan in Plan mode, which the tester reviews and approves before anything runs.

### Step 4: Exploring the Screen(Action)

Claude opens the feature in a browser, through Claude in Chrome or a Playwright MCP server, and learns how it works.

### Step 5: Writing and Running the Tests(Action)

Claude creates positive, negative, and boundary test cases and automation code, then runs the tests.

### Step 6: Triaging Failures (Verification)

Claude sorts each failure into a script bug, an environment issue, or a product defect. It fixes only script bugs and reports the rest. It never edits a test to match behavior the acceptance criteria do not describe.

### Step 7: Reporting(Action)

Claude sends the test results to TestRail and updates the Jira ticket, both through connectors.

### Step 8: Automation

The process can also be configured to run automatically every night as a routine that posts a summary to Slack.

Other common use cases across IT teams include:

- Explaining an unfamiliar legacy codebase to a new developer
- Large-scale code migrations spread across hundreds of files,a good fit for dynamic workflows
- Automatic review of every pull request through a Routine
- Turning requirements documents into positive, negative, and boundary test cases
- Monitoring a deployment every hour and alerting on failure
- A weekly defect digest emailed before anyone logs in on Monday

## Benefits of the Claude Ecosystem

- Flexible Access: Use Claude through different tools and workflows.
- Easy integration: MCP is an open standard, so anyone can connect internal systems.
- Flexible Automation: Adopt exactly as much automation as your risk tolerance allows, from approving every plan to running routines overnight.
- Built-in Validation: Plans, checkpoints, hooks, and evaluator models all exist to check the work.
- Reusable Team Knowledge: Team knowledge becomes reusable through skills and CLAUDE.md, a project file Claude Code reads at the start of every session.
- Enterprise Security: Provide sandboxing, permission gates, SSO, and no training on business data.

## Limitations of the Claude Ecosystem

- Some features are experimental: Several headline features, including Computer Use, are still research pr

# Claude vs. ChatGPT: 5 key differences that could change which AI you use

Knowing what makes each AI agent special is part of knowing how to use them

Share this article

Join the conversation

Follow us

Add us as a preferred source on Google

Subscribe to our newsletter

ChatGPT and Claude are two of the biggest names in AI, and both have become significantly more capable within the last few months. Whether you need help writing an email, researching a topic, creating an app or managing your workload, both chatbots can handle far more than simple questions and answers. But despite their similarities, OpenAI and Anthropic have taken different approaches to building their AI assistants.

ChatGPT has evolved into an all-purpose assistant with tools for everything from image generation and voice conversations to coding and research. Claude has become hyper-focused on writing, programming and helping users complete more complicated tasks through its growing collection of productivity tools.
Now that Anthropic has gone public, people are beginning to wonder what is so special about the company's AI known as Claude.

I've spent plenty of time testing both, and while there's considerable overlap between what they can do, there are some differences worth understanding before deciding which one deserves your time and money.

Latest Videos FromTom's Guide

Here are five of the biggest differences between Claude and ChatGPT.

## 1. Claude has an edge in natural writing

Claude has developed a reputation for producing natural-sounding text that is especially true for longer pieces. It's also good at following detailed writing instructions and maintaining a consistent tone and style across multiple rounds of editing.

And while ChatGPT is no slouch when it comes to writing, either, it has the advantage of flexibility. You can ask it to rewrite something in five different tones, brainstorm headline ideas or transform a complicated explanation into something a beginner can understand.
So, while Claude may be the better starting point for someone writing a novel or polishing a lengthy document, ChatGPT is especially useful when experimenting with different approaches.

Of course, writing quality is subjective. The results also depend on which model you're using and how clearly you explain what you want.

Want more AI news?

Sign up to the Tom's AI Guide weekly newsletter summing up all the biggest AI news you need to know. Plus, analysis from our AI editors and tips on how to use the latest AI tools!

## 2. You can create images with ChatGPT

One of ChatGPT's biggest advantages is how many different types of tasks it can handle within the same experience.

Alongside traditional text conversations, ChatGPT supports image generation and editing. You can describe a picture you want to create, upload an existing image to change its appearance or use the chatbot to develop visual concepts.

ChatGPT also offers voice conversations, so users can speak naturally with the assistant instead of typing everything into a chat window.

Claude has expanded its creative capabilities, too, particularly through Artifacts, which lets users create interactive content, visualizations and applications.

However, Claude's creative tools are more focused on building useful digital experiences than generating standalone images.

For anyone who regularly switches between writing, visual creation and spoken conversations, ChatGPT offers a more versatile experience.

## 3. Claude Code and OpenAI's Codex code differently

Coding or "vibe coding" has become one of the biggest battlegrounds between Anthropic and OpenAI.

Claude Code is Anthropic's coding agent, designed to work directly with codebases, understand existing projects, make changes and help developers solve complicated programming problems.

It has become particularly popular with developers who want an AI assistant that can work inside their existing development environment.

OpenAI's answer is Codex, which can also navigate repositories, write code, fix bugs and handle development tasks.

Both tools go well beyond generating snippets of code in a chatbot. They can take on larger assignments and work through multiple steps of a project.

The biggest difference is often how developers prefer to work. Claude Code has strong roots in terminal-based development, while Codex offers workflows across different development environments and agent-based tasks.

For casual users who occasionally need help building a website or debugging a script, either chatbot can be useful. Developers working on larger projects may find that their preferred coding agent becomes the deciding factor.
Personally, I tend to hit my usage limits and blast through tokens faster with Claude Code,

## 4. Claude is leaning into the AI coworker concept

One of the most interesting changes to Claude is Anthropic's growing focus on turning the chatbot into a coworker.

With Cowork, Claude can take on more complicated assignments involving files, documents and connected tools. Rather than walking through every step in a conversation, users can describe the outcome they want and let Claude work through the assignment.

For example, someone could ask Claude to organize project materials, work through a collection of documents or prepare files for a presentation.

ChatGPT is moving in a similar direction with its own agent capabilities, including ChatGPT Work and Codex.

The difference is how these experiences are organized and presented to users. Anthropic has emphasized the idea of Claude as a digital coworker that can take responsibility for larger assignments. OpenAI has built a broader ecosystem that includes conversational assistance, research, creative tools and specialized agents.

Neither approach is inherently better, but if you're looking for an AI assistant to do more than answer questions, knowing the difference is important.

## 5. ChatGPT has a cheaper entry-level subscription

Price is another consideration, particularly if you're not sure how often you'll use an AI chatbot.

Both companies offer free access, although usage limits and available features vary.

ChatGPT Plus and Claude Pro each cost $20 per month in the United States. ChatGPT also offers a lower-priced Go subscription for $8 per month, giving users another option between the free and Plus tiers.

Claude offers annual billing for Pro, which can reduce the effective monthly cost for users willing to commit to a full year.

Of course, usage limits, access to more powerful models and included tools can make one subscription more valuable than another. For example, if you think you're going to be creating more images and want that type of creativity from a model, than you'll want to go with ChatGPT.
At the same time, if you're a casual user looking for an affordable upgrade, ChatGPT offers more flexibility in its pricing. But, if you rely heavily on Claude's writing and coding capabilities, Pro may be worth the investment.

## Final thoughts

Here's some good news: you don't have to choose between one or the other. Because ChatGPT offers so much for free, it might be worth sticking with it. But, if you find yourself going through tokens much faster with Claude, you might want to consider bumping up your subscription to a paid tier.
I use both agents for different things, which brings me to another point. The bigger question is what you want your AI assistant to do.

Claude is particularly appealing for people who spend their days writing, coding or working through complicated projects. Its emphasis on natural language and increasingly capable agent tools makes it a strong choice for serious productivity work.

ChatGPT offers a broader experience. Between image generation, voice conversations, research, coding and its growing collection of productivity features, it's designed to serve as an assistant for almost anything.

If you want one AI chatbot that can handle the widest variety of everyday tasks, start with ChatGPT. If your priorities are writing, coding and managing complex workflows, Claude deserves a serious look. And since both offer free versions, the easiest way to decide is to give them the same five prompts and see which one delivers the results you actually prefer.

# OpenAI Opens GPT-Live-1.1 API With Cheaper Voice Standby

Developers can now use ChatGPT’s GPT-Live-1.1 voice model, with improved multilingual speech and a lower rate when calls are on standby.

### Key Notes

- OpenAI has released GPT-Live-1.1 in the API after introducing the model in ChatGPT Plus and Pro in October, with claimed improvements in multilingual speech and transcription.
- WebRTC sessions can enter standby after a configurable idle period, reducing the voice duration rate from five cents to two cents per minute during those pauses.
- The voice model can keep a conversation going while a separate backend performs work, with backend model and tool usage billed separately.

OpenAI has opened GPT-Live-1.1 to developers, bringing the voice model already used in ChatGPT to applications built through its API. The release targets assistants that can hold a conversation while an AI agent looks up information or completes work in the background.

The November 19 API changelog announces improvements in multilingual pronunciation, accent consistency and transcription. OpenAI also introduced a cheaper standby setting for quiet stretches of a call, addressing the cost of keeping a voice assistant available between requests.

### ChatGPT’s Voice Model Moves Into Other Apps

GPT-Live-1.1 can listen and speak simultaneously, allowing a person to interrupt, add a detail or change direction before the assistant finishes its reply. OpenAI says it handles precise information such as letters and numbers more reliably, an important distinction for conversations involving names, addresses or account references.

The model has powered voice in ChatGPT Plus and Pro since October 15, according to the developer announcement. The new release extends that capability to developers usinggpt-live-1.1. It builds on the full-duplex approach we covered when the GPT-Live family launched in July.

OpenAI’s model documentation lists audio and text as supported inputs and outputs. The API model does not accept images or video, so its availability should not be read as a release of every capability found elsewhere in the ChatGPT app.

### Standby Cuts the Cost of Quiet Time

GPT-Live-1.1 costs $0.05 per active minute and $0.02 per standby minute, with voice sessions billed by the second. That makes the standby duration rate 60% lower than the active rate. Backend model and tool charges remain separate, according to OpenAI’s pricing.

Standby is available for both GPT-Live-1 and GPT-Live-1.1 over WebRTC. Developers can set an idle timeout between five and 60 seconds, after which inference pauses while the connection stays open. The conversation resumes when the user speaks again.

The session guide notes that conversation history is restored on resumption, although the first response to a short utterance may take longer. Developers must configure the timeout: if it is omitted, inference remains active after the first wake until the session ends.

### Conversation and Execution Have Separate Jobs

GPT-Live handles the spoken exchange and delegates reasoning or tool use to a backend. That backend can be a configured OpenAI Responses model or a developer’s own model, agent or service. An illustrative customer-service workflow could keep talking to a caller while a separate system checks an order and returns its status.

The delegation documentation assigns permissions, required confirmations and business records to the application. Developers therefore still decide which operations an assistant may perform and when a user must approve them. A more natural voice does not establish that an underlying transaction was authorized or completed.

For businesses, the combination is more consequential than an accent upgrade alone. A voice interface that remains responsive during background work can make an agent easier to use, while standby reduces the duration charge during pauses. The practical measure is whether the complete service understands the request, finishes the task correctly and keeps the total cost acceptable.

# OpenAI tests Dots agents for ChatGPT Plus subscribers — Engadget

UA.NEWS  20 November 2026 09:42

OpenAI has begun testing Dots personal AI agents among a limited number of users of the $20-per-month ChatGPT Plus plan. Previously, the feature was available on more expensive plans starting with ChatGPT Pro. Engadget reports on the expansion of access.

## Agents can work autonomously

Dots are proactive agents that can independently perform tasks and continue working even when the user is not interacting with them. They have access to OpenAI’s plugin ecosystem, enabling them to interact with more than 4,000 apps.

The agents can also connect to the user’s computer, control it on their behalf, and work alongside them. Task progress can be tracked by opening the agent’s virtual “computer.”

More current news is available on the UA.News Telegram channel Telegram.

## Terms for other plans

According to ChatGPT engineering lead Thibaut Sottiaux, Dots are set to become available to all ChatGPT Business Standard users starting today. For Pro and Business Premium subscribers, interaction with agents does not count toward standard ChatGPT usage limits if the tasks are not complex.

At the same time, OpenAI did not clarify whether this condition will apply to Plus and Business Standard users. For Plus owners, access may become available starting today, but the company has not yet said whether this will be a permanent update.

Dots initially ran on the GPT-6 Astra model and now also support GPT-6.1 Terra. OpenAI has added iOS widgets, Shortcuts integration, iMessage and RCS support, as well as the ability to respond to iOS notifications.

# ChatGPT Dots Reach Plus and Business Standard Users as OpenAI Tests a New Mobile Design

OpenAI started testing dots, its proactive always-on ChatGPT agents, with a small number of Plus users and began rolling them out to eligible Business Standard members in the US on 19 November 2026. A redesigned ChatGPT mobile app with a dedicated dot tab is starting with Pro users.

OpenAI is bringing dots, its always-on personal agents in ChatGPT, to cheaper plans. The company has started testing dots with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users and is rolling them out to eligible Business Standard members in the United States. At the same time, OpenAI is testing a redesigned ChatGPT mobile app in which each user’s dot gets its own tab.

i10X Quick Take

## Quick Take

- Plus test: dots are being tested with “a small number of ChatGPT Plus users,” OpenAI’s Thibault Sottiaux posted on 19 November 2026.
- Business Standard: OpenAI’s release notes say dots are rolling out to eligible Business Standard members in the US, with one personal dot per member and usage limits.
- New mobile design: a bottom tab bar with a dedicated dot tab, and users can pin Codex, Projects, Images and more.
- Who gets the redesign first: Pro users who have a dot or can create one, plus a small group of eligible Plus users.
- Not in Europe: dots are not available in the European Economic Area, the UK or Switzerland.

## In plain English

A dot is a ChatGPT helper that keeps working on your tasks in the background, even when you are not chatting with it. Until now it was mainly for the most expensive plans. OpenAI is now letting some people on the $20 Plus plan and many small business teams try it. The phone app is also getting a new layout so your dot and favorite tools are one tap away.

## What happened

Sottiaux, who works on Codex and ChatGPT at OpenAI, wrote on X late on 19 November: “Heads up, we’re starting to test dots with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users.” He added: “We’re also bringing dots to all ChatGPT Business Standard users. Rollout will start today.”

Heads up, we’re starting to test dots with a small number of ChatGPT Plus users. Looking forward to the continued feedback as we expand and I’m recently seeing a lot more positives around how good the proactivity has been after many improvements.
Tibo (@thsottiaux) · November 19, 2026 · View on X
OpenAI’s ChatGPT Business release notes for 19 November confirm the rollout “to eligible ChatGPT Business Standard members in the United States,” where each member can create one personal dot in the Business workspace for tasks such as preparing a weekly update.

Minutes later, Sottiaux shared the new app: “We’re also working on a new mobile experience for ChatGPT!” He said it starts with Pro users who have a dot or are eligible for one, that “Some of you will see the new experience by default,” and that it can be switched in Settings under New ChatGPT Design.

## Background

OpenAI launched dots as persistent agents on GPT-6 Astra in late September, with each dot running on its own cloud computer and connecting to thousands of apps. Since then OpenAI has added more models, control of a user’s own computers and payments through ChatGPT Wallet. Enterprise, Edu and Healthcare workspaces got dots by default from 18 November unless an admin opts out, according to OpenAI’s help center.

## What’s in the redesign

- Tab bar: the preview video shows a Home tab with an “Ask anything” field, a dedicated dot tab and a grid of other tools.
- Pinning: users can “pin Codex, Projects, Images, and more to the tab bar,” Sottiaux wrote. Digital Trends reported that the grid also lists Scheduled, Plugins, Finance, Health and Sites.
- Regions: Digital Trends, citing OpenAI, reported that the redesign excludes the EEA, the UK, Switzerland and South Korea.
- Toggle: eligible users can turn the new design on or off in Settings.

## Why it matters

For Plus subscribers, a test on the $20 plan is the clearest sign yet that OpenAI wants proactive agents to be a mass-market feature rather than a premium add-on.

For small businesses, Business Standard access gives every eligible member one agent for recurring work, which makes dots a team productivity tool, not just a personal one.

For the assistant market, putting the agent in its own tab turns ChatGPT’s app from a chat window into a home screen for tasks. That raises the pressure on rivals building similar always-on agents, such as Meta’s Muse and Google’s Gemini.

## What’s still open

- OpenAI has not said how many Plus users are in the test or whether access will stay after it ends.
- Usage limits for Business Standard dots were not published in detail.
- There is no timeline for availability in Europe, the UK or Switzerland.

## Sources

- Thibault Sottiaux (@thsottiaux) posts on X, 19 November 2026
- OpenAI Help Center: ChatGPT Business release notes (19 November 2026) and “Getting started with your dot”
- Digital Trends, 19 November 2026; Engadget and The Verge, 20 November 2026

## i10x Perspective

Dots started as a showcase for OpenAI’s most expensive plans. Moving them down to Plus and Business Standard shows the company now sees background agents as the default way people will use ChatGPT. The open issue for users is trust: an agent that acts on its own needs clear limits and an easy way to check its work. More on this in Browsers & Assistants.

# OpenAI begins testing ChatGPT dot with Plus users and expands Business access

OpenAI is rolling out ChatGPT dot testing to select Plus subscribers and expanding availability for business users. Here is what is new.

·1 min read

OpenAI has officially started testing its proactive AI assistant, ChatGPT dot, with a small group of ChatGPT Plus subscribers. Previously, the feature was limited to Pro, Business Premium, and Enterprise tiers.

Key highlights: - Testing expands to select ChatGPT Plus users. - Powered by GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Terra models. - Features its own cloud computer and operates 24/7.

## Capabilities and Ecosystem of ChatGPT dot

Introduced in September, ChatGPT dot is designed as an always-on assistant capable of handling ongoing tasks, working across connected apps, and making progress on projects independently. It connects to over 4,000 apps via plugins.

Earlier this month, OpenAI added the GPT-6.1 Terra model alongside GPT-6 Astra to power the feature. Additionally, custom instructions were recently introduced, allowing users to define how their dots behave and respond.
Read alsoChatGPT spontaneously resets reasoning mode from High to Medium

## Business Expansion and Usage Limits

Alongside the Plus rollout, OpenAI is expanding access for business users. Any work delegated through ChatGPT Work or Codex counts toward the standard allowances for those specific subscription tiers.

The development team notes positive feedback regarding the assistant's proactivity following recent performance improvements across the platform.

## What This Means for the Industry

Bringing proactive AI agents to the Plus tier marks a significant step toward mainstream adoption of autonomous software assistants. Developers and professionals can leverage these tools to handle complex, multi-step workflows across diverse cloud applications effortlessly.

# SemiAnalysis撤回「Gemini完了」判断，向Google DeepMind道歉

SemiAnalysis发文撤回「Gemini is cooked」判断，承认此前看衰Google模型有误。

半导体与AI研究机构SemiAnalysis在社交平台X上发布了一份写给Google DeepMind主席Demis Hassabis的「道歉表」，正式撤回其今年8月对Google大模型前景的悲观判断。这份表格以半开玩笑的方式列出多个「认错理由」，包括「只看了X上的消息」「被在Anthropic工作的室友说服」「没有阅读模型卡」等，最后一行则写道：关于Gemini 4，他们错了，只想从当初的标题里撤回一个词——把「Gemini is cooked」（Gemini完了）改成「Gemini这回真做出了点东西」。

事件的起点是今年8月SemiAnalysis发布的一篇看空报告。该文认为，Google自去年11月短暂领先之后，再未发布令人兴奋的模型，已处于掉队状态。报告分析称，DeepMind强化学习团队流失不少人，内部算力分配也不理想，并给出相当重的判断：Google当然还会继续发布模型，但再一次达到行业最高水平的概率已经「降到了零」。

然而报告发出后不到两个月，Google便公布了Gemini 4 Argon，随后在10月底发布Carbon、11月12日推出Hydrogen、18日发布Neon，短短8天内接连推出三款模型。其中Carbon的表现一度登上Artificial Analysis综合能力榜首。这些模型在社交媒体上收获大量好评：主打Flash的Hydrogen在写作和复杂软件任务上能快速完成，最智能的Carbon擅长处理各类长程Agent任务，而介于两者之间的Neon兼顾速度与智能，被认为是Gemini 4系列中综合能力最强的一款。X上大量用户点赞了「Gemini 4 Neon太疯狂了」「解决了此前对Gemini模型的所有不满」等评论。

11月，Google DeepMind研究员Arthur Douillard在X上透露，团队曾把那篇批评文章打印出来放在桌上，每天提醒自己当时的问题确实存在，并感谢SemiAnalysis的「激励」。SemiAnalysis随后转发该帖并晒出这份道歉表，几小时后Hassabis转发接梗，表示「接受道歉」，同时打趣对方漏勾了「低估了Google DeepMind这群高手」这一项。实际上，在机构官号发梗图两周多前，8月看空报告的共同作者Dylan Patel就已在Gemini 4 Carbon评测发布后，以个人名义向Google公开致歉。

从被公开唱衰到连续发布四款模型并重返榜单前列，Google内部经历了怎样的调整？回溯今年夏天，唱衰并非毫无来由：原定6月推出的Gemini 3.5 Pro迟迟未上线，Google CEO桑达尔·皮查伊曾在5月的I/O大会上预告该模型6月推出，但最终未能如期发布。受限于算力约束，加上多位项目负责人之间存在意见分歧，编程等后来至关重要的方向在当时获得的资源偏少。此后接掌研发的Koray Kavukcuoglu也解释称，团队那一阶段把更多注意力放在了迭代较快的Flash模型上。

在内部资源博弈与外界质疑声中，Google于8月5日宣布对DeepMind进行重大组织调整：原DeepMind CTO、Google首席AI架构师Koray Kavukcuoglu出任DeepMind高级副总裁，直接向皮查伊汇报，全面负责Gemini模型开发、前沿研究以及Gemini应用和开发者团队；Demis Hassabis交出日常运营职责，转任DeepMind主席和Alphabet首席科学家；与此同时，Gemini原技术共同负责人Jeff Dean、Oriol Vinyals与Sanjay Ghemawat、Quoc Le一同离开谷歌，创办了Discovery Loop。

外界常以为Google既不缺数据也不缺芯片，做不成大模型难以理解。但即便拥有自研AI芯片TPU，训练下一代Gemini要用，给眼前用户生成答案要用，Google Cloud的客户也在排队。对集团而言，芯片卖出去是好生意；对研究员而言，排不上的实验就是做不了。据外媒报道，谷歌云高管也希望Koray接掌DeepMind后，能缓和内部在TPU供应分配上的紧张关系。

不过，若把Gemini 4的爆发全部归功于8月的人事调整和算力安排，显然低估了大模型研发的长周期规律。公开记录显示，早在8月5日组织调整和8月7日看空报告发布之前，Gemini 4的底座工程就已经在进行中。在2026年7月22日的Alphabet二季度财报电话会上，皮查伊明确透露，Gemini 4已经启动了「Google迄今最有野心的预训练」，管理层已将大量算力和精力集中投入，目标是依托这一代基础模型加快迭代，将发布节奏推进到接近每月一版。Koray后来在9月初与11月19日的两场播客访谈中进一步还原了研发机制：DeepMind内部实行多条研发线并行推进，当一组人打磨当前发布版本时，另外两组团队已在同步开发后续两代模型，因此10月看到的Gemini 4背后有至少一年的连续研发沿革。

如果说大规模预训练与多线并行提供了底座，那么让Gemini 4在编程与智能体执行上取得明显突破的，是一套基于真实工程场景的后训练体系。2026年11月12日，时任Gemini后训练负责人的Melvin Johnson在AI Engineer CODE大会上，以SemiAnalysis的批评文章开场，详细披露了Google内部的训练方法。首先是用内部真实工作流替代静态公开题库：Google内部每天约有10万名员工使用编程工具Antigravity写代码，后训练团队每训练出几个候选模型版本，就会在内部发起盲测，让工程师用自己手头的真实开发任务去检验、挑选更顺手的版本。模型在跨文件修改中哪一步卡住、哪一次改坏了既有逻辑，这些真实的「失手现场」会被立刻回收，转化为下一轮训练题与评分细则。与此同时，团队会果断淘汰「过期题目」——在强化学习中，一旦模型对某道题反复尝试都能稳定拿满分，每次采样得到的奖励信号完全相同，模型就无法从中分辨「哪种做法更好」，这类题目必须撤下，换成更高难度的挑战。

其次，团队重新定义了什么叫「做完了」，并重点关注智能体的诚实度。传统代码评测中，只要跑通单元测试就能拿分；但在Gemini 4的后训练评分里，团队不仅看功能是否实现，还会考察边界条件处理、代码质量、改动范围是否克制以及后续可维护性。更重要的是，评分系统会把模型的「自我汇报」与它的实际操作日志逐一核对：如果一道难题只完成了一半，模型如实交代进度依然可以获得部分奖励；但如果它连测试都没运行就声称「全部通过」，就会遭到严厉惩罚。Johnson提到，此前Google内部一项高难度工程评测中，基线模型的编造率为8%，Hydrogen约为3%，Carbon约为1.5%。

凭借扎实底座和高强度后训练，Google从9月底到11月中旬的短短七周内连续公布了四款Gemini 4系列模型。其中Hydrogen和Neon都是从Carbon适配出来的：Carbon瞄准需要长时间推理的难题，Hydrogen追求日常任务的执行速度，Neon则兼顾推理深度和效率。回过头看，SemiAnalysis当时指出的很多问题确实存在，DeepMind的研究员也没有否认。只是三个月后的结果证明，外界还是低估了Google多年积累的研发能力，以及它把这些能力集中投入到一代模型上的速度。眼下的Gemini 4，又成了其他模型必须认真面对的竞争对手——Google不仅把编程、Agent等能力重新推到了第一梯队，也开始在真实的用户使用和产品体验上追赶Codex、Claude等Agent产品。对用户而言，主要厂商竞争越激烈，越有机会用上更便宜、更可靠、更容易访问的AI。

事件的起点是 2026 年 8 月 SemiAnalysis 发布的一篇看空报告。该报告认为，Google 自去年 11 月短暂领先之后，再未发布令人兴奋的模型，已处于掉队状态。报告分析称，DeepMind 的强化学习团队流失了不少人员，内部算力分配也存在问题，并给出一个相当重的判断：照此下去，Google 仍会继续发布模型，但再次达到行业最高水平的概率已经「降到了零」。

然而，报告发出不到两个月，Google 便公布了 Gemini 4 Argon，随后在 10 月底发布 Carbon、11 月 12 日推出 Hydrogen、18 日发布 Neon，短短 8 天内接连推出三款模型。其中 Carbon 在 Artificial Analysis 的综合能力榜单上登顶。这些模型在社交媒体上收获大量好评：主打 Flash 的 Hydrogen 在写作和复杂软件任务上能快速完成；最智能的 Carbon 擅长处理各类长程 Agent 任务；介于两者之间的 Neon 则兼顾速度与智能，被认为是 Gemini 4 系列中综合能力最强的一款。

面对外界的批评，Google DeepMind 研究员 Arthur Douillard 在 X 上透露，团队曾把那篇批评文章打印出来放在桌上，每天提醒自己当时的问题确实存在，并感谢 SemiAnalysis 提供的动力。随后 SemiAnalysis 转发了这条帖子，并晒出了开头那份道歉表。几小时后，Hassabis 转发接梗表示「接受道歉」，同时打趣说对方漏勾了「低估了 Google DeepMind 这群高手」这一项。事实上，在机构官号发梗图的两周多前，8 月看空报告的共同作者 Dylan Patel 就已在 Gemini 4 Carbon 的评测发布后，以个人名义向 Google 公开致歉。

从 8 月初被权威机构公开唱衰，到 11 月中旬连续推出四款 Gemini 4 系列模型并重返榜单前列，Google 内部经历了怎样的调整与积累？

回到今年夏天，唱衰并非毫无根据。原定 6 月推出的 Gemini 3.5 Pro 迟迟未能上线，Google CEO 桑达尔·皮查伊 曾在 5 月的 I/O 大会上预告该模型于 6 月推出，但最终未能如期发布。受限于算力约束，加上多位项目负责人之间存在意见分歧，编程等后来显得至关重要的方向在当时获得的资源偏少。此后接掌研发的 Koray Kavukcuoglu 也解释称，团队在那一阶段把更多注意力放在了迭代较快的 Flash 模型上。

在内部资源博弈与外界质疑声中，Google 于 8 月 5 日宣布对 DeepMind 进行重大组织调整：原 DeepMind CTO、Google 首席 AI 架构师 Koray Kavukcuoglu 出任 DeepMind 高级副总裁，直接向皮查伊汇报，全面负责 Gemini 模型开发、前沿研究以及 Gemini 应用和开发者团队。Demis Hassabis 交出日常运营职责，转任 DeepMind 主席和 Alphabet 首席科学家。与此同时，Gemini 原技术共同负责人 Jeff Dean、Oriol Vinyals，与 Sanjay Ghemawat、Quoc Le 一同离开谷歌，创办了 Discovery Loop。

外界常有疑问：Google 既不缺数据也不缺芯片，为何做不成大模型？但即便拥有自研 AI 芯片 TPU，训练下一代 Gemini 需要算力，给眼前用户生成答案需要算力，Google Cloud 的客户也在排队。对集团而言，芯片卖出去是好生意；对研究员而言，排不上的实验就是做不了。据外媒报道，谷歌云高管也希望 Koray 接掌 DeepMind 后，能缓和内部在 TPU 供应分配上的紧张关系。

如果把 Gemini 4 几款模型爆发并广受好评的功劳都算在 8 月的人事调整和算力安排上，显然低估了大模型研发的长周期规律。公开记录显示，早在 8 月 5 日组织调整和 8 月 7 日看空报告发布之前，Gemini 4 的底座工程就已经在进行中。在 2026 年 7 月 22 日的 Alphabet 二季度财报电话会上，皮查伊明确透露，Gemini 4 已经启动了「Google 迄今最有野心的预训练」。他表示，管理层已将大量算力和精力集中投入到 Gemini 4 上，目标是依托这一代基础模型加快后续迭代速度，将发布节奏推进到接近每月一版本。

Koray 后来在 9 月初与 11 月 19 日的两场播客访谈中进一步还原了 Gemini 4 的研发机制：DeepMind 内部实行多条研发线并行推进，当一组人打磨当前发布版本时，另外两组团队已经在同步开发后续两代模型。因此，10 月看到的 Gemini 4 背后有至少一年的连续研发沿革。

如果说大规模预训练与多线并行提供了底座，那么让 Gemini 4 在编程与智能体执行上取得明显突破的，是一套基于真实工程场景的后训练体系。2026 年 11 月 12 日，时任 Gemini 后训练负责人的 Melvin Johnson 在 AI Engineer CODE 大会上，以 SemiAnalysis 的批评文章开场，详细披露了 Google 内部的训练方法。

首先是用内部真实工作流替代静态公开题库。Johnson 透露，Google 内部每天约有 10 万名员工使用编程工具 Antigravity 写代码。每当后训练团队训练出几个候选模型版本，就会在内部发起盲测，让工程师直接用自己手头的真实开发任务去检验、挑选更顺手的版本。模型在跨文件修改中哪一步卡住、哪一次改坏了既有逻辑，这些真实的「失手现场」会被立刻回收，转化为下一轮训练题与评分细则。与此同时，团队会果断淘汰「过期题目」：在强化学习中，一旦模型进化到对某道题反复尝试都能稳定拿满分，每次采样得到的奖励信号完全相同，模型就无法从中分辨「哪种做法更好」，这类题目必须撤下，换成更高难度的挑战。

其次是重新定义什么叫「做完了」，并重点关注智能体的诚实度。在传统代码评测中，只要跑通单元测试就能拿分；但在 Gemini 4 的后训练评分里，团队不仅看功能是否实现，还会考察边界条件处理、代码质量、改动范围是否克制以及后续可维护性。更重要的是，评分系统会把模型的「自我汇报」与它的实际操作日志逐一核对。如果一道难题只完成了一半，模型如实交代进度依然可以获得部分奖励；但如果它连测试都没运行就声称「全部通过」，就会遭到严厉惩罚。Johnson 提到，此前在 Google 内部一项高难度工程评测中，基线模型的编造率为 8%，Hydrogen 约为 3%，Carbon 约为 1.5%。

凭借扎实底座和高强度后训练，Google 从 9 月底到 11 月中旬的短短七周内连续公布了四款 Gemini 4 系列模型。其中 Hydrogen 和 Neon 都是从 Carbon 适配出来的：Carbon 瞄准需要长时间推理的难题，Hydrogen 追求日常任务的执行速度，Neon 则兼顾推理深度和效率。

回过头看，SemiAnalysis 当时指出的很多问题确实存在，DeepMind 的研究员也没有否认。只是三个月后的结果证明，外界还是低估了 Google 多年积累的研发能力，以及它把这些能力集中投入到一代模型上的速度。眼下的 Gemini 4，又成了其他模型必须认真面对的竞争对手。Google 不仅把编程、Agent 等能力重新推到了第一梯队，也开始在真实的用户使用和产品体验上，追赶 Codex、Claude 这些 Agent。对行业观察者而言，头部模型厂商之间竞争加剧，往往意味着算力投入增加、模型能力迭代加快，最终可能让用户用上更便宜、更可靠、更容易访问的 AI 服务。

# Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 4 Neon for Paid Users

Google DeepMind is rolling out Gemini 4 Neon to developers, businesses and paid Gemini subscribers. The model can process spreadsheets, documents, audio and video, and Google says it leads a coding-agent benchmark. Developers will pay based on the amount of data sent to and generated by the model.

Google DeepMind is releasing Gemini 4 Neon to developers, businesses and paid subscribers, bringing a new model to the Gemini app and API.

Access depends on the product. Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can select Neon in the Gemini app, while businesses can use it through Gemini for business.

Google says Neon handles coding, research and analytical tasks. It can process spreadsheets, PDFs, charts, audio and video together and turn them into structured documents.

## Pricing and access

Developers can use Neon through the paid Gemini API tier in Google AI Studio and Android Studio. The API is a way for developers to connect their software to the model.

Google charges $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output tokens. Tokens are units used to measure the text or other data a model processes and generates.

Cached input tokens cost $0.15 per million, a 95% discount. The model has a 1 million-token context window, the amount of information it can consider in a session.

Paid Google AI Pro and Ultra subscribers can also try Neon in Google Antigravity. Businesses can access it through the Gemini for business API or model menu, and through Google Antigravity.

## Coding and research benchmarks

Google says Neon ranked first on the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, with a score of 58.6. That benchmark assesses models on coding tasks carried out by agents.

The model also scored 65.2% on Terminal-Bench 4.1 and 46.2% on FrontierCode 2.0 at its default high setting, Google said. The company says Neon can debug and revise code across multiple files.

On the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, Neon scored 61 at its xhigh thinking level and ranked third overall, according to Google. The company said it placed behind larger, slower models.

Google reported a second-place ranking on the Vals Index, with a score of 70.9%. It also said Neon ranked first on the Legal Research Bench and Tax Agent Bench.

Neon has four thinking levels, which let teams adjust the amount of processing used for a task. Google says the default high level costs 32% less per task than Carbon on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index.

## Cybersecurity and safety claims

Google says Neon scored 76% on the hard tier of AutoBaxBench, which tests secure code generation. It also scored 51.26% on WebExploitBench v1.2, a test related to finding security flaws.

The company says Neon resisted every attack in a Gray Swan benchmark when it used real-time safeguards at its highest thinking level. The test plants malicious instructions in material a model accesses, such as web pages or documents.

Google says eligible members of its Fairwind Program will begin receiving access to Neon for cyber defense over the next few days.

Google.title: Google DeepMind 推出 Gemini 4 Neon：七週內第四款模型，速度近倍而價格更低 - HKAIWeb News
Google.description: Google DeepMind 已於 2026 年 11 月 18 日發布 Gemini 4 Neon，是該公司七週內推出的第四款模型，官方定位為以快速端到端任務完成提供前沿級智慧，面向複雜軟體工程、知識工作與科學研究流程。公告由
Google.content:
跳至內容

Google DeepMind 已於 2026 年 11 月 18 日發布 Gemini 4 Neon，是該公司七週內推出的第四款模型，官方定位為以快速端到端任務完成提供前沿級智慧，面向複雜軟體工程、知識工作與科學研究流程。公告由 Google DeepMind 高級副總裁暨 Google 首席 AI 架構師 Koray Kavukcuoglu 發表。

定價方面，Gemini 4 Neon 的輸入價格為每百萬 token 3 美元（快取輸入 0.15 美元，享有 95% 折扣），輸出價格為每百萬 token 15 美元，並配備 100 萬 token 上下文視窗。第三方基準機構 Artificial Analysis 的實測顯示，Neon 在 xhigh 推理檔位的生成速度約為每秒 110 個 token，接近 Gemini 4 Carbon（約 57 個 token）的兩倍，同一基準的處理時間亦由約 36 分鐘縮短至約 21 分鐘。

官方公布的基準結果包括：在 Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index 的 xhigh 檔位取得 61 分，總排名第三，僅次於規模更大、速度更慢的模型；Vals Index 以 70.9% 排行第二，落在 Pareto 前沿；在新推出的 Agent Arena Index 中，Neon 以 1,336 分在全球排行第二，評估涵蓋 4,200 多個真實代理工作階段，可控性（steerability）同樣排行第二，並在內部 Google Antigravity 測試中錄得迄今最低的捏造率。其他領先項目包括 Legal Research Bench 與 Tax Agent Bench 均列第一、Zapier AutomationBench 取得 56.3% 排行第一、Vending-Bench 2 以 16,843 美元營業額排行第一，以及 Terminal-Bench Science（70.5%）、RiemannBench（84.0%）與 HLE-Diamond（71.3%）等科學與數學基準。

獨立報導同時提醒定價比較的細節。據 The Decoder 引述 Artificial Analysis 數據，Neon 的定價較 Gemini 4 Carbon 的常規價格（每百萬 token 輸入 4 美元、輸出 20 美元）低 25%，但較 Carbon 在 11 月 30 日前的促銷價格高 50%；在 xhigh 檔位，Neon 每項任務成本約 6.44 美元，較 Carbon 的 7.76 美元低約 17%，而節省完全來自較低的單價，因為 Neon 每項任務實際比 Carbon 多產出約 15% 的 token。該報導亦指出，Google 自家的比較表只列入 Claude Opus 5.5 與 GPT-6.2 Sol，並未包含排在總榜前兩位的 GPT-6.2 Astra 與 Claude Fable 5.2。在編碼任務方面，Neon 在 Coding Agent Index 取得 59 分，高於 Carbon 的 55 分以及 Claude Fable 5.2 與 Claude Opus 5.5 的 58 分，平均每項編碼任務成本為 6.86 美元。

供應情況方面，Gemini 4 Neon 已開始推出：開發者可在 Google AI Studio 與 Android Studio 經 Gemini API 付費層使用；企業可透過 Gemini for business（API 或模型下拉選單）與 Google Antigravity 調用；Google AI Pro 與 Ultra 訂閱者則可在 Gemini app 選用。面向網絡防禦的 Gemini 4 Neon for cyber 將於未來數日經 Fairwind Program 向受信任的防禦者推出。

同日，Google 亦更新了搜尋首頁：產品副總裁 Robby Stein 宣布於桌面版首頁新增可摺疊側邊欄，用戶可以查看及繼續過往以 AI Mode 進行的對話，亦可開啟新對話串、搜尋對話記錄或連結 Gemini Notebook；此功能正在全球桌面端陸續推出。

# Meta AI的答案能相信嗎？專家解析資訊來源、查核盲點與使用建議

查核記者／曾慧雯；責任編輯／陳偉婷

前文回顧：用Meta AI查證反被誤導？ Threads AI屢次答錯，連選舉謠言也當真
為了更深入瞭解Meta AI「已讀亂回」現象背後運作的機制，查核中心採訪陽明交通大學人工智慧學院智慧產業與綠能研究所副教授許志仲、國家資通安全研究院研究員曾仲毅。

許志仲表示，Meta AI早期主要採用Meta自行開發的Llama系列模型，但Meta超級智慧實驗室於2026年4月發表新模型Muse Spark後，官方宣布將逐步應用於Meta AI及旗下各社群平台。因此，Threads於5月底開放使用者標註Meta AI時，當時採用的模型資訊已指向Muse Spark；不過，由於Meta並未公開每一則回覆實際使用的模型版本，後台也可能隨時調整，實際上外界無法逐一確認每次回答究竟由哪個版本生成。

許志仲說明，Muse Spark主要有三大特色。第一，它與Llama模型不同，並未提供外界下載使用，研究者無法自行取得模型測試；第二，它具備看圖能力；第三，也是它最大的特色，就是跟Meta自家平台綁很深，官方稱Muse Spark可以引用 IG、FB、Threads上的公開貼文來回答。許志仲說，這一點是Muse Spark方便的地方，但也是它被用於查核上最大的風險，因為社群平台上的內容不一定正確，如果AI引用的資料本身就有問題，得出的答案也可能有誤。

許志仲表示，目前不同AI模型用於一般追溯或查核工作上，表現應該都差不多，主要差別應該只在於這些AI模型的資訊來源為何。由於Meta沒有公開它撈資料的完整機制，因此只能根據官方說法及實際表現推測，其資料庫來源可能包括模型訓練時學到的知識（有截止時間）、即時搜尋到的網頁，以及 Meta平台上的公開貼文。

曾仲毅也研判，由於Threads內建的Meta AI是免費服務，不見得願意承擔額外風險，所以其資料庫範圍可能比較保守，一方面可控制成本，另一方面也能避免Meta AI被用於肉搜、竊取個資等不當用途。

至於Meta AI會不會參考原始貼文底下的留言來作答？雖然官方沒有明講，但許志仲指出，這類系統要回答「這篇是真的嗎？」，就得把該篇貼文跟相關討論一起丟給模型參考，留言很可能就包括在內。

問題是，語言模型的回答高度仰賴輸入資料，它比較像在「整理大家怎麼說」，因此，如果網路上充斥相同的謠言，AI就可能將謠言整理成看似有條理的懶人包，反而助長錯誤資訊傳播。Meta AI官方也提醒，AI的回覆可能會不準確或不適當，因此不該用於做出重要決策。

### AI易受提問方式影響，且查核圖片、影片及新謠言的準確度有限

此外，許志仲引用國外研究說明，AI可能出現迎合提問者的傾向。他表示，西班牙查核組織Maldita.es與哈恩大學在2026年10月針對社群平台X的AI聊天機器人Grok進行研究，發現當使用開放式問法時，回答錯誤率約為59.7%；若直接詢問內容是否正確，錯誤率則降至17.4%。研究者認為，這可能與AI傾向迎合提問者的預設立場有關。

這項研究也發現，當新謠言剛出現、尚未有查核報告時，AI特別容易出錯。在研究測試的38則說法中，有16則出現「同一則訊息前後回答矛盾」的情況，其中多達15則發生在相關查核報告出現之前。

也就是說，利用AI協助查核時必須特別注意，當一則錯誤訊息剛開始流傳，網路上能搜尋到的資料可能幾乎都是謠言本身時，AI若缺乏可靠資訊交叉比對，就可能將錯誤內容當成事實，反而讓謠言升溫。許志仲提醒，這種風險確實存在，而且因為AI的回覆在留言區公開顯示，會讓民眾覺得「AI都這樣說了」，其影響力比一般留言還大。

Threads內建的Meta AI究竟可不可信？許志仲表示，目前他還沒看到專門針對Threads上的系統性評測，比較能參考的是同類研究，以前述Grok研究為例，在317則回答中，59.9%正確、26.8%錯誤、13.2%答對一部分；但文字型的說法正確率有95.8%，圖片和影片則只有49.4%，落差很大。

許志仲指出，今年8月美國公共廣播電台（NPR）跟專門評估新聞與資訊網站可信程度的NewsGuard合作，共測試了包含Meta AI在內的6個聊天機器人，整體表現不差，但評價其實不見得一定準確，跟實際使用的體感可能會略有不同，例如Meta AI就有過「已讀亂回」的紀錄，把冒用法國雜誌《Le Point》名義的假影片說成是該雜誌的報導。

許志仲提醒，AI聊天機器人並非完全不能用，但文字型、已經有查核報告的訊息，通常比較容易找到可靠資料；相較之下，圖片、影片、人物辨識、剛發生的新聞，以及高度在地化的台灣議題，都可能出現判斷錯誤的情況，而且AI即使答錯或出現幻覺，依然可能使用肯定語氣回覆，讓使用者難以察覺異狀。

### AI查核應當作進一步查證線索，而不是最終判斷

對一般使用者而言，許志仲建議，應把AI的回答當作進一步查證的線索，而非直接視為真假判決，尤其在查證圖片、影片時，不要相信AI說「這是真的」或「這是AI做的」，因為這部分的辨別就連使用專業工具都不容易做到，聊天機器人的判斷更不可靠。

由於提問方式也會影響AI的回答，因此許志仲建議盡量採取中性問法，例如「這個說法是真的嗎？有哪些證據？」而不是已經預設傳言為真。同一個問題重複詢問，也可能得到不同答案，例如前述Grok研究中，Grok對同一則貼文回答超過一次的40則貼文中，就有21則前後說法不一。

許志仲也建議，如果是剛爆出來的消息，應先等官方說明或事實查核組織的查核報告。至於平台方面，他認為至少要清楚附上來源，不輕易對圖片、影片下真假結論，以及把專業查核的結果接進來，提供給使用者足夠的參考依據。

Meta.description: The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. ... This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.
Meta.content:
# Meta Model API

The Meta Model API (public preview) serves Meta Superintelligence Labs' Muse Spark models through an OpenAI-compatible API. The Meta provider extends the OpenAI provider and supports its compatible options.

note

This provider uses the Meta Model API atapi.meta.ai for Muse models. Meta retired the separate Llama API at api.llama.com on July 6, 2026.

## Setup

- Create an API key from the API keys tab on the Meta Model API dashboard.
- Set theMODEL_API_KEY environment variable, or specify apiKey or a custom apiKeyEnvar in your config.

providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3

meta:<model> defaults to the Responses API — Meta's full-feature surface and the one its docs recommend. Use meta:chat:<model> for the OpenAI-compatible chat completions endpoint, or meta:messages:<model> for the Anthropic-compatible Messages API. If you omit the model, the provider defaults to muse-spark-1.1; select muse-spark-1.3 explicitly to use the latest model.

## Available Models

Check the models page for the live list. As of writing:

- muse-spark-1.3 — latest model for coding and agentic workflows, with a 1,048,576-token context window, text/image/video/PDF input, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.
- muse-spark-1.3-contributor — the same model with discounted pricing. Selecting this ID permits Meta to use your prompts and completions to train future models.
- muse-spark-1.1 — original Muse Spark model, still supported.

Both 1.3 IDs work with the Responses, Chat Completions, and Messages APIs. Meta notes that audio understanding in 1.3 is not fully supported and may produce degraded responses.

## Configuration
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: high
      max_completion_tokens: 8192
      temperature: 1.0

### Configuration Options

The provider accepts compatible OpenAI provider options. Notable behavior:

- reasoning_effort — minimal, low, medium, high, or xhigh. When omitted, the model picks its own reasoning depth. Muse Spark does not support none; the provider rejects it with a clear error. Reasoning tokens bill at the output rate and count toward the output cap.
- max_completion_tokens — caps generation on the chat endpoint (Meta accepts max_tokens only as a deprecated alias; if you set it, the provider forwards it as the canonical max_completion_tokens). On the Responses API the cap is max_output_tokens, and the provider maps max_completion_tokens/max_tokens onto it. When unset, no cap is sent so reasoning can use the full output budget.
- temperature — supported (0–2, API default 1.0). Promptfoo sends its deterministic default of 0 unless you override it.
- response_format — structured output with guaranteed JSON schema matching.
- tools / tool_choice — parallel tool calling with streamed arguments.
- prompt_cache_retention — in_memory or 24h for prompt caching; cached prompt tokens bill at the cached-input rate.
- seed — best-effort determinism.

On Chat Completions and Responses, promptfoo rejectslogprobs, n > 1, stop, and logit_bias before sending a request. It also rejects stream because these integrations expect a complete JSON response. OpenAI-scoped environment defaults (OPENAI_TEMPERATURE, OPENAI_TOP_P, OPENAI_MAX_COMPLETION_TOKENS, penalty variables) are not applied to Meta requests.

### Cost Tracking

Promptfoo computes token cost from Meta's published pricing, including the discounted rate for cached input:

Model | Input / 1M | Cached input / 1M | Output / 1M 
---|---|---|---
muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.1 | $1.25 | $0.15 | $4.25 
muse-spark-1.3-contributor | $0.10 | $0.002 | $0.20 

Contributor pricing requires opting into Meta's training data terms by selecting the Contributor model ID. Override token prices withcost, inputCost, outputCost, or cacheReadCost (USD per token) for custom rates. Token cost excludes web-search charges.

## Responses API

meta:<model> (the default) and meta:responses:<model> target Meta's /v1/responses endpoint — the only Meta endpoint that carries reasoning across turns, with built-in web-search grounding:
providers:
  - id: meta:responses:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium
      tools:
        - type: web_search

Withweb_search, the model grounds answers in real-time web results with inline citations. Web search bills separately ($2.50 per 1,000 queries) and is not included in promptfoo's computed token cost.

## Messages API

meta:messages:<model> targets Meta's Anthropic-compatible Messages endpoint (https://api.meta.ai/v1/messages) — the surface Anthropic-format coding agents such as Claude Code use. Use it to evaluate Muse Spark over the same wire format those agents send:
providers:
  - id: meta:messages:muse-spark-1.3
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192

The provider extends the Anthropic provider, so its options (max_tokens, tools, image and document content blocks, etc.) apply. It defaults max_tokens to 131,072 and enables streaming so the Anthropic SDK can safely handle long generations; streamed output is aggregated before grading. Authentication uses your Meta key as a bearer token (Authorization: Bearer), matching Meta's docs — Anthropic-scoped settings like ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL, ANTHROPIC_MAX_TOKENS, ANTHROPIC_TEMPERATURE, custom headers, and Claude Code OAuth credentials are deliberately ignored on this surface.

Muse Spark's reasoning arrives on this surface as encryptedredacted_thinking blocks, so the provider defaults showThinking to false to keep the ciphertext out of graded output.

## Using with coding-agent providers

Meta positions Muse Spark as a backend for coding agents, and promptfoo's agentic providers can evaluate those setups end to end. In both recipes, setapiKey explicitly: the agent subprocesses inherit your shell environment, and an explicit key guarantees your Meta key is used instead of an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY or ANTHROPIC_API_KEY that belongs to another service.

### Codex CLI

Theopenai:codex-sdk provider drives Muse Spark over the Responses API:
providers:
  - id: openai:codex-sdk
    config:
      base_url: https://api.meta.ai/v1
      model: muse-spark-1.3
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'

The explicitapiKey is required — the provider does not read MODEL_API_KEY on its own, and without it an ambient OPENAI_API_KEY would be sent to the Meta endpoint instead.

### Claude Code

Theanthropic:claude-agent-sdk provider forwards config.env to the agent subprocess. Pass the environment Meta's guide prescribes, with apiKey set to your Meta key:
providers:
  - id: anthropic:claude-agent-sdk
    # Provider-level `env` outranks the eval's top-level `env`, pinning the
    # routing values a suite-wide ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL (e.g. an Anthropic
    # gateway) would otherwise override — which would send the Meta key there.
    env:
      ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
      ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
    config:
      apiKey: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
      env:
        ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL: https://api.meta.ai
        ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN: '{{env.MODEL_API_KEY}}'
        ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS: ''
        ANTHROPIC_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_OPUS_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_SONNET_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ANTHROPIC_DEFAULT_HAIKU_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        CLAUDE_CODE_SUBAGENT_MODEL: muse-spark-1.3
        ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH: 'true' # Claude Code disables MCP tool search for non-first-party hosts

warning

Do not omitapiKey, the empty ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS override, or the provider-level env block. The provider forwards its resolved API key into the agent subprocess as ANTHROPIC_API_KEY after env: is applied — if apiKey is unset and a real ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is exported in your shell, that Anthropic credential would be transmitted to Meta's endpoint. Clearing ANTHROPIC_CUSTOM_HEADERS prevents an inherited gateway or proxy secret from being sent to Meta. The provider-level env block matters because the subprocess environment is layered process.env < config.env < provider/suite env: without the pin, a top-level env.ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL in the same config would silently re-route the agent — and your Meta key — to that URL.

Pin every model alias as shown — Claude Code otherwise routes background tasks, Plan Mode, or subagents to Claude models the Meta API doesn't serve. See Meta's coding agents guide for the full setup pattern.

## Example Usage
providers:
  - id: meta:muse-spark-1.3
  - id: openai:gpt-5.5

prompts:
  - 'Summarize the following in one sentence: {{text}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      text: 'Promptfoo is an open-source tool for testing and evaluating LLM apps.'

Get started with a runnable example:
npx promptfoo@latest init --example provider-meta

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.meta.ai/v1 (override with apiBaseUrl; the Messages surface uses the bare host https://api.meta.ai).
- OpenAI-compatible chat completions (/chat/completions) and Responses (/responses) endpoints, plus the Anthropic-compatible Messages (/messages) endpoint.
- Rate limits apply per team, not per key: 3,000 RPM / 4M TPM for Standard models and 100 RPM / 3M TPM for Contributor models.
- Full API documentation.

## 由 kaiyuan_wang 于 11月 15 日 发布

有风声说 Meta 打算重新回到开源模型这条路上，Llama 那条线可能要复兴。

听到这个我心情有点复杂。这家当年靠开源把整个本地部署生态盘活了，一大批工具链、微调方案、量化格式都是围着它长出来的。后来路线摇摆，重心往闭源那边挪，社区那股劲一下就散了，主力阵地慢慢转到别家去。

现在传回归，好事，但得看诚意。是真放权重、放许可证，还是放个阉割版意思意思。开源这事最怕的不是不做，是做一半——大家投入时间围着你建生态，你中途变卦，二次伤害比一开始就不做还狠。

另外时机也变了。现在开源这一档已经有几家跑在前面了，回来不是重新称王，是得先证明自己还配上桌。

你们还会为这条线再投入一次吗？

DeepSeek.content:
# DeepSeek’s computing crunch pushes China’s AI developers beyond models

As computing bottlenecks force DeepSeek to restrict user usage, China’s AI race is entering a pragmatic new phase: less about building bigger models, and more about monetising agents and enterprise tools.

20 Nov 2026

Economy

(By Caixin journalist Yang Zirui)

DeepSeek has begun restricting conversations and document reading on its website and app because of insufficient computing capacity, exposing a constraint that is pushing China’s leading AI developers to seek growth beyond large models.

Since 15 November, individual users have encountered company notices saying that long conversations inactive for 72 hours can no longer be processed by DeepSeek because of a shortage of computing resources. When processing long-form documents, DeepSeek has also warned that it can read only the first 20 pages of a document or 10,000 tokens, citing the same reason.

The restrictions have drawn complaints in the comments beneath the latest post on DeepSeek’s official Xiaohongshu social media account. Some users asked the company to remove the limits, saying that they would be willing to pay for a subscription. Unlike competing services such as Doubao and Kimi, DeepSeek does not offer a paid membership for individual consumers, charging instead for usage through its application programming interface (API) services.

The pace of improvement in Chinese foundational models has slowed considerably, narrowing the differences between them. — Yao Shuqiao, Chief AI Analyst, Haitong International

The computing squeeze comes as Chinese AI laboratories slow the pace of foundational model advances and put more emphasis on agents, software tools and enterprise partnerships to find new sources of growth. Their emerging contest is less about topping performance rankings than about delivering usable results — and generating revenue without relying solely on ever-larger models.

## Growth constraint

DeepSeek has fewer computing resources than major cloud providers and needs to allocate them efficiently, giving paying customers priority for the most effective service, Yao Shuqiao, chief AI analyst at Haitong International, told Caixin. The usage restrictions allow the company to differentiate how it supplies those resources, Yao said.

Yao expects computing power for Chinese models to remain tight in the short- and medium-term. As products improve and usage rises, with industrial applications entering a more demanding phase in 2027, demand for computing resources is expected to grow exponentially, Yao said, adding that recent overseas developments involving Nvidia Corp. could also increase the risk of a broader cutoff of China’s access to advanced computing chips.

Concern about that risk has already been reflected, to some extent, in the shares of two Hong Kong-listed Chinese model developers, Z.AI Co. Ltd. and MiniMax Group Inc. Z.AI closed at HK$335 (US$43) on 17 November, down 5.3% that day and 32.9% over four trading days, reaching its lowest level in six months. MiniMax closed at HK$116, falling 7.1% that day and 35.6% over four trading days, after sliding below its previous post-listing low.

Xiao Rui, an AI expert, compared the [large language] model to a horse and the harness to the equipment people use to guide and constrain it.

Z.AI’s most recent flagship model release dates to mid-August. MiniMax has yet to release the Pro model it has described as being trained with about 3 trillion parameters.

DeepSeek is not alone in facing computing pressures. Moonshot AI abruptly suspended new subscriptions when it introduced Kimi K3 in July because of computing power shortages. After launching Kimi K3.1 Pro in late October, it apologised to users for rate limits and unnecessary consumption of usage allowances associated with the new model.

DeepSeek released DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on 10 September and updated it on 17 October, but has not introduced a V4.1 Pro version. When Moonshot AI released Kimi K3.1 Pro on 24 October, it described it as the first model in the K3.1 series. So far, Moonshot AI has not released an upgraded version from K3.1 Pro.

As model releases slow, Chinese developers are expanding their revenue opportunities through agent-control frameworks, application tools and enterprise cooperation.

The pace of improvement in Chinese foundational models has slowed considerably, narrowing the differences between them, Yao said. Developers are increasingly competing over the completeness of their ecosystems rather than concentrating primarily on improvements to model capabilities.

## Making models work

One focus is the harness: the operating and control layer surrounding a model that helps it reliably complete complex, multistep tasks through AI agents.

Xiao Rui, an AI expert, compared the model to a horse and the harness to the equipment people use to guide and constrain it. In AI, the term encompasses the components outside the model that make it usable, he told Caixin.

The industry often describes an agent as a model plus a harness. Yao said that the harness establishes mechanisms that allow a model to keep executing tasks, turning its capabilities into automated productivity.

DeepSeek introduced its harness on 13 August alongside the release of DeepSeek-V4-Pro. DeepSeek Harness adopts what the company described as an “everything is a plugin” approach: the agent’s capabilities are assembled from interchangeable components that can be reorganised. DeepSeek also made the harness’s source code available under the MIT licence.

That design has attracted attention because, unlike frameworks primarily optimised for their developers’ own models, DeepSeek’s is more accommodating of third-party models, Xiao said.

Yao said that DeepSeek Harness supplies open-source infrastructure for running agents, lowering barriers to participation. It can also be jointly optimised with DeepSeek models for functions such as tool use and context management, strengthening their competitiveness while drawing developer community traffic to the company.

## Get the ThinkChina Weekly Newsletter

Insights on China, right in your mailbox. Sign up now.

By subscribing, I agree to SPH Media's Terms and Conditions and Privacy Policy.

DeepSeek has updated its harness to support each new model release. On 29 September, it introduced a desktop version for DeepSeek Harness with functions for office work and software development.

According to the company, DeepSeek Harness’ daily active users reached about 1.5 million by 4 November, a 545% increase from the launch of its desktop version, with daily token consumption standing at about 92 trillion.

Efficiency is an important reason behind Chinese model developers’ increasing bet on harnesses. Yao said that a smaller model optimised through a harness can, in some routine agent tasks, deliver close to 90% of a larger model’s capabilities at about 4% of the cost. Changes to self-verification, execution tracing and context optimisation alone can significantly improve coding agent performance, Yao added.

In the agent era, companies want to secure users not only for foundational models but also for their ecosystems and toolchains. — Yao

Xiao characterised harness development principally as an engineering challenge rather than a computing capacity challenge. That makes it easier for Chinese developers to catch up with US competitors than in foundational models, Xiao said.

## Building a commercial ecosystem

DeepSeek is also widening the range of its API services it sells to developers. On 13 November, the company announced application APIs covering capabilities including online search, search with deeper reasoning, file input and model safety. It also offered access to underlying functions such as text and image search, webpage retrieval, text recognition, speech recognition and speech synthesis.

The company said that developers could use the suite to build complex conversational functions into their own applications.

The services create additional sources of revenue. Beyond token charges, DeepSeek levies fees for the underlying tools. For example, text or image searches and webpage retrieval each cost 5 RMB (US$0.70) per 1,000 calls, while text recognition costs 1.5 RMB per 1,000 pages.

In the agent era, companies want to secure users not only for foundational models but also for their ecosystems and toolchains, Yao said. DeepSeek’s application APIs are intended to attract traffic through its open-source ecosystem and make developers more likely to stay, supporting both long-term ecosystem development and monetisation.

## Pursuing enterprise customers

Enterprise business is becoming another central growth route. According to a Menlo Ventures report released in November, Chinese models accounted for 89% of US enterprise spending on open-source models, with Kimi models being most popular among them.

Kimi K3, released in July and trained with 2.8 trillion parameters, was the largest open-source model by parameter count at the time and became a representative of the frontier capabilities of Chinese models.

Sun Wei, chief AI analyst at market research firm Counterpoint, told Caixin that Kimi K3’s customised open-weight licence, which sets commercial use conditions, and its enormous size mean that it is currently more focused on expanding its enterprise customer base.

Companies that once competed over benchmark scores are increasingly confronting a different purchasing decision: customers are not paying for the model itself, but for the results it produces.

DeepSeek.content:
# DeepSeek

DeepSeek provides an OpenAI-compatible chat API. The provider accepts OpenAI chat options; DeepSeek determines which options each model supports.

## Setup

- Get an API key from the DeepSeek Platform
- SetDEEPSEEK_API_KEY environment variable or specify apiKey in your config

## Configuration

Basic configuration example:
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-flash
    config:
      max_tokens: 4000
      passthrough:
        thinking: { type: disabled }

  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      max_tokens: 8192
      showThinking: true
      passthrough:
        thinking:
          type: enabled
        reasoning_effort: high

### Configuration Options

- temperature
- max_tokens
- reasoning_effort - none disables thinking; low, high, and max enable it. DeepSeek defaults to high. When neither max_tokens nor OPENAI_MAX_TOKENS is set, Promptfoo uses DeepSeek's output budget.
- cost, inputCost, outputCost, cacheReadCost - Set cost estimates in USD per token. inputCost and outputCost take precedence over cost; cacheReadCost sets a separate cached-input rate.
- top_p, presence_penalty, frequency_penalty
- showThinking - Control whether reasoning content is included in the output (default: true, applies to thinking-capable models)

Promptfoo requests complete responses; this provider does not support streaming.

## Available Models

DeepSeek listsdeepseek-flash and deepseek-v4-pro in its model catalog. The older deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner IDs are retired. The shorthand deepseek: uses deepseek-flash with thinking disabled; use the full ID for DeepSeek's default thinking mode.

### deepseek-flash

Usedeepseek:deepseek-flash for V4.1 Flash, which supports text and image inputs. The older deepseek-v4-flash and deepseek-v4-flash-vision-exp IDs route to the same model. It supports a 1M-token context window and up to 384K output tokens.

### deepseek-v4-pro

V4 Pro supports text input, thinking and non-thinking modes, a 1M-token context window, and up to 384K output tokens.

DeepSeek charges different peak and off-peak rates. Promptfoo estimates current models at peak rates: Flash costs $0.30 input, $0.006 cached input, and $1.20 output per million tokens; Pro costs $1.32, $0.044, and $3.96 respectively. Off-peak rates are half these amounts. SetinputCost, outputCost, and cacheReadCost in USD per token to override the estimate using the current rates. Promptfoo does not infer the billing period or Chinese public holidays.

warning

Sampling support differs by mode.temperature has no effect in thinking mode. top_p only affects thinking mode and values below 0.95 are treated as 0.95. See the Chat Completions reference for parameter limits.

## Example Usage

Compare DeepSeek with OpenAI on a reasoning task:

promptfooconfig.yaml
# yaml-language-server: $schema=https://promptfoo.dev/config-schema.json
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      max_tokens: 8000
      showThinking: true # Include reasoning content in output (default)
  - id: openai:gpt-5.4-mini
    config:
      reasoning_effort: medium

prompts:
  - 'Solve this step by step: {{math_problem}}'

tests:
  - vars:
      math_problem: 'What is the derivative of x^3 + 2x with respect to x?'

### Controlling Reasoning Output

SetshowThinking: false to exclude reasoning content from the output:
providers:
  - id: deepseek:deepseek-v4-pro
    config:
      showThinking: false # Hide reasoning content from output
      passthrough:
        thinking:
          type: enabled

WithshowThinking: true (the default), the output includes reasoning when DeepSeek returns it:
Thinking: <reasoning content>

<final answer>

WithshowThinking: false, assertions see only the final answer. This option does not turn off thinking at the API; use config.passthrough.thinking: { type: disabled } for that.

## API Details

- Base URL:https://api.deepseek.com/v1
- OpenAI-compatible API format
- DeepSeek API documentation

## See Also

- OpenAI Provider - Compatible configuration options
- Historical MMLU comparison - Replace its retired provider IDs with the current IDs shown above before running it.

DeepSeek限额与开放同行，梁文锋到底想做什么？

铑科技 2026-11-20 09:55:37

21320

分享到

作者 | 鸿辰

DeepSeek突然限额了！

先别着急把梁文峰从“梁圣”切换成“梁子”，这背后值得深度研究。

相信很多DeepSeek用户都发现了，App和网页版出现了新的使用限制，超过一定时间没有活跃的长对话不能用了。连续对话一段时间，就可能出现“服务器繁忙，使用额度已达上限”的提示。

DeepSeek又怎么了？是用户太多，服务器又扛不住了吗？

据OpenRouter数据显示，11月9日至15日这一周，DeepSeek V4.1 Flash的Token调用量已经达到59.2万亿，位居全球第一。

但是，就在这几天，DeepSeek又干了一件非常耐人寻味的事，它把自己的能力彻底交给了开发者，宣布正式开放“全家桶应用API”。

什么意思呢？就是以前你在DeepSeek App里联网搜索、上传文件、阅读网页、进行语音交互等这些看起来是一个聊天软件的功能。

现在，DeepSeek全部拆出来给开发者自由调用。

甚至官方直接给开发者提供了一个开源Demo，基于这些能力，外部用户完全可以做出一个接近完整DeepSeek App的产品。

一边限制额度，另一边又鼓励大家去用，梁文锋到底想做什么？

据天眼查App显示，今年7月，杭州深度求索人工智能基础技术研究有限公司完成工商变更，新增股东包括国家人工智能产业投资基金、杭州程砺企业管理咨询合伙企业，梁文锋本人也参与了此次增资。在此之前，DeepSeek完成了一轮规模达510亿元的融资。

就在上个月，DeepSeek又完成了超千亿的融资。过去的DeepSeek只是一个产品，现在它正在变成一种别人产品背后的AI能力。看起来只差几个字，实际上完全是两回事。

如果DeepSeek把搜索、阅读、文件解析、语音这些能力全部开放出来，你做教育软件、做办公软件，做各种Agent，甚至自己做一个AI助手，都可以把DeepSeek当成底层能力。

未来，终端用户甚至不需要知道，原来我用的是DeepSeek的能力。

一个模型最强的形态，不一定是让所有人都来下载它的App。还有一种可能，就是让所有App都来调用它。

这恰恰也可以解释，为什么最近DeepSeek的算力压力这么大。

当然，我们不能直接说梁文锋要“放弃C端用户”，也不能把这次限额直接解释成DeepSeek已经确定要转型。

但至少有一个事实非常明确，DeepSeek正在把原本属于App的能力，大规模API化。而DeepSeek认为，现有的对话产品只是比较基础的一种形态。

翻译成大白话就是，聊天框可能只是开始，真正值得想象的是模型能力被开发者重新组合之后，会变成什么。

所以，别急着把DeepSeek这次限额理解成“它不行了”。DeepSeek可能正在从一个“你每天打开的AI产品”，变成一个“别人每天调用的AI基础设施”。

前者争的是用户，后者争的是生态。而一旦进入生态竞争，真正的问题就不再是谁的App下载量高，而是谁的大模型被更多的产品采用。

这可能才是梁文锋真正想要回答的问题，而这也是真正值得关注的信号。你觉得呢？

DeepSeek.content:
